svg.title: Tributech Modbus Source device hierarchy and TCP connection sharing
svg.desc: A single Tributech Modbus Source can hold up to fifty Modbus Devices. The source itself, identified as source:modbus;3, carries no connection settings. Each child device, identified as device:modbus;1, carries its own connection settings: Device A connects to host modbus-server-a on port 5020 with unit identifier 1; Device B connects to the same host modbus-server-a on port 5020 with unit identifier 2; Device C connects to host modbus-server-b on port 5020 with unit identifier 255. Every device owns its own streams and parameters: Device A, shown expanded, has a Modbus Stream, identified as stream:modbus;2, reading HoldingRegister 100, and a Modbus Parameter, identified as parameter:modbus;2, holding HoldingRegister 200 at a configured value. Devices B and C have their own streams and parameters, not itemised here. On the right, TCP connections are counted per endpoint rather than per device or per source. Device A and Device B both target the endpoint modbus-server-a:5020, so their two lines converge into one shared line: a single TCP connection is opened, and the unit identifier is sent with each individual request to distinguish the two devices. Device C targets a different endpoint, modbus-server-b:5020, and therefore opens its own single TCP connection. In short: one TCP connection per distinct host and port combination, shared by every device that points at the same endpoint.
svg.text: One source, many devices, one connection per endpoint
A Modbus Source holds up to 50 devices. Each device carries its own connection settings and owns its streams and parameters.
shared by Device A and Device B
One connection per distinct Host:Port — devices on the same endpoint share it.
